newsitem.title: CHINA: Gas explosions in central China mines kill 86.
newsitem.headline: Gas explosions in central China mines kill 86.

text.p: A series of explosions in a group of coal mines in central China killed at least 86 people and injured 12 last week, local officials said on Tuesday.
The blasts, which tore through tunnels at the Pingdingshan mines in an area of Henan province about 760 km (460 miles) south of Beijing, were caused by gas in the coal shafts, the officials said.
One official said 98 people had been in the mines when the gas exploded, killing all but 12. None of the injured were in critical condition, he said.
The explosions occurred in three separately operated mines in Henan province, officials said. One mine had two shafts and the others had one each, all of which were connected underground.
"There are old tunnels underground that link the four shafts, when an explosion happened in one it set off blasts in the others," said one local official.
"This is the worst such accident on record in Henan province," another official said by telephone.
The owners of the privately-run mines were in custody, he said, but gave no details.
Chinese media regularily report serious accidents in the nation's thousands of often small and poorly regulated coal mines, despite repeated official campaigns for stricter safety measures.
